description: specs/verification-architecture.md's own Pure Core declaration for `nextRerouteState` (the state machine verification-architecture.md itself calls 'the SOLE arbiter of every retry/reroute/escalation branch decision', and which Phase 5's purity-audit.md claims to have independently re-verified 'matches declared' with 'zero deviations') does NOT match the actual shipped implementation. Declared (verification-architecture.md:93-96, Pure Core section): `nextRerouteState({ attemptsUsed, maxAttempts, lastOutcome })` returning `{ shouldRetry: boolean, excludeSlot: string|null, exhausted: boolean }`. Actual implementation (runtime/loop/always-act-router.mjs:148-153): `nextRerouteState({ attemptsUsed, maxAttempts })` -- no `lastOutcome` parameter exists anywhere in the function or any of its call sites -- returning `{ shouldRetry: boolean, attemptsUsedNext: number, exhausted: boolean }` -- no `excludeSlot` field is ever produced. This is independently confirmed by the raw test-runner output itself: verification/proof-harnesses/full-suite-run.txt line 47 reads 'nextRerouteState: attemptsUsed===0 -> shouldRetry true, attemptsUsedNext 1, exhausted false; attemptsUsed===1 -> shouldRetry false, exhausted true (maxAttempts=1)' -- confirming `attemptsUsedNext` (not `excludeSlot`) is the real second field, and no `lastOutcome` input is exercised anywhere. Every one of `index.mjs`'s 4 call sites of `nextRerouteState` (lines 702, 718, 816) passes only `{ attemptsUsed, maxAttempts: 1 }`, never a third `lastOutcome` argument. verification-architecture.md was actively maintained through 4 spec-review-driven Changelog entries (iterations 1-4) but this function-shape description was never reconciled against the actual Phase 2b/2c implementation, and Phase 5's own purity-audit.md (section 'Mismatches found', line 120-129) explicitly and incorrectly asserts 'None. Every item in the declared Purity Boundary Map was independently re-derived this session (fresh reads + greps, not merely re-quoting Phase 1b's own claims) and matches.' That self-certification is factually false for this specific, named function -- the purity-audit session apparently verified the ABSENCE of I/O and judgment-branching (which does hold) but did not actually diff the declared function SIGNATURE/return-shape against the real one it claims to have read in full.

evidence.snippet: `nextRerouteState({ attemptsUsed, maxAttempts, lastOutcome })` -- REQ-505/506/511/513: pure bounded-retry state machine (`{ shouldRetry: boolean, excludeSlot: string|null, exhausted: boolean }`) -- the single shared counter (`maxAttempts = 1`) enforcing REQ-511's ceiling...

additionalEvidence.snippet:
## Mismatches found

**None.** Every item in the declared Purity Boundary Map was independently re-derived this session (fresh reads + greps, not merely re-quoting Phase 1b's own claims) and matches.
nextRerouteState: attemptsUsed===0 -> shouldRetry true, attemptsUsedNext 1, exhausted false; attemptsUsed===1 -> shouldRetry false, exhausted true (maxAttempts=1)
const state = nextRerouteState({ attemptsUsed, maxAttempts: 1 }); -- three call sites, none ever pass a third `lastOutcome` argument.

recommendation: Update specs/verification-architecture.md's Pure Core `nextRerouteState` entry to the actual shipped signature/return shape (`{attemptsUsed, maxAttempts}` -> `{shouldRetry, attemptsUsedNext, exhausted}`, no `lastOutcome`/`excludeSlot`), and correct purity-audit.md's 'zero deviations' claim to either be accurate or explicitly disclose this one deviation as harmless (behavior is correct; only the Phase 1b design doc's literal signature/shape description is stale). This is a documentation-accuracy fix only -- no source/test change is implied, since the actual implementation and its tests are internally consistent and correct.
